title: Al-Sharaa Meets Trump and Erdoğan on Sidelines of NATO Ankara Summit
detail: President Ahmad al-Sharaa attended the 2026 NATO summit in Ankara (July 7–8) as a guest, holding sideline meetings with US President Donald Trump and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan on July 8. At a joint news conference with Trump, al-Sharaa credited US sanctions relief and backing from Turkey and Gulf allies for Syria's progress on 'national consolidation' over the prior year and a half. Erdoğan and al-Sharaa held closed-door talks on bilateral relations and regional developments at the presidential complex in Ankara. A previously planned Washington meeting between Trump and al-Sharaa had been cancelled the prior month, with the White House citing scheduling reasons.

media.caption: Erdoğan and al-Sharaa hold talks in Ankara as the NATO summit provides a diplomatic backdrop for Syria's outreach

title: Trump Moves to Rescind Syria's State Sponsor of Terrorism Designation
detail: Secretary of State Marco Rubio notified Congress on July 8, 2026 that President Trump had decided to rescind Syria's designation as a state sponsor of terrorism — a status imposed on Syria in the late 1970s under Hafez al-Assad and the last major remaining western sanction on Damascus. Trump outlined the rescission process in a letter to al-Sharaa signed during the NATO summit in Ankara; the move now faces a 45-day congressional review window, which a Republican-controlled Congress is expected to approve. Analysts said the change would let Syria reconnect to the international banking system and unlock direct trade, though banking-infrastructure and investor-confidence hurdles remain.

media.caption: Syria is on the cusp of a sanctions-free era after Trump moved to rescind its state sponsor of terrorism designation
